title: Redux Thunk
description: Learn async logic with Redux Thunk middleware.

data.text: **Redux Thunk** is middleware that allows you to write action creators that return **functions** instead of plain action objects. This enables asynchronous logic like API calls, waiting for timers, or accessing state before dispatching.

A **thunk** is a function that wraps an expression to delay its evaluation. In Redux terms, a thunk allows you to dispatch a function that can execute async code and dispatch other actions. The thunk receives `dispatch` and `getState` as arguments.

terms.definition: A function that delays an operation by wrapping it in another function.
Operations that affect the outside world: API calls, timers, DOM changes.
A function provided to thunks to read the current Redux state.
Actions that return promises, allowing chaining and handling async completion.

data.title: Redux Toolkit createAsyncThunk
data.content: The modern way to handle async with thunks

cards.title: Redux Thunk
cards.content: Simple concept: return functions from action creators. Good for basic async: single API calls, simple chains. Easier to learn.

cards.title: Redux Saga
cards.content: Uses generator functions and declarative effects. Better for complex flows: parallel operations, cancellation, polling. Steeper learning curve.

data.title: Modern Recommendation
data.text: For most applications, use createAsyncThunk from Redux Toolkit. It handles loading states, errors, and the action lifecycle automatically.

Mixing manual thunk writing with createAsyncThunk unnecessarily

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Thunks allow action creators to return functions for async logic
Thunks receive dispatch and getState as arguments
createAsyncThunk is the modern Redux Toolkit approach
Best for simple to moderate async flows; use Saga for complex flows
data.takeaway: Redux Thunk is the standard middleware for handling asynchronous operations in Redux, with createAsyncThunk being the recommended modern approach.
